title: Out-of-sample test of ordering by the small-noise coefficient, alpha_inter=0.45
purpose: Test whether, within a richness level, the shared-to-independent ratio of mean squared CV in balanced (mixed, equal-K, r0=1) communities is predicted beyond the small-noise regime by monotone interpolation in x = c * sigma_env^2, where c is the second-order small-noise coefficient, using new competition and autocorrelation values.
rationale: In the three sigma_mechanism grids, the floor-free ratios were perfectly rank-ordered by x within each richness level (Spearman 1.0, 1.0, 0.999 for S = 2, 4, 8). This pattern was noticed after those grids ran, so it is tested here on new alpha_inter and phi values.

Predictions for every cell were computed before running and are stored in analysis/prespecified/ordering_predictions_2026-10-19.json, with the reference curve taken from analysis/reports/fig7_mechanism_reversal_summary.csv.
S = 12 is outside the reference richness levels and tests a directional prediction only.
acceptance_checks: The combined parquet validates against the manifest with 1000 replicates per scenario.
Floor occupancy is reported for every cell; cells with any retained floor contact are flagged and excluded from the accuracy criterion, not dropped.
